papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.
papers.reason: Investigates resonant $s$-channel scattering of neutrinophilic dark matter with neutrinos inside supernovae, directly intersecting supernova neutrino physics and BSM searches.

summary.tldr: Resonant $s$-channel scattering between neutrinophilic dark matter and supernova neutrinos efficiently traps sub-GeV dark matter within the protoneutron star, opening an unconstrained parameter window in conventional supernova cooling limits.
summary.novel_idea: Prior supernova cooling constraints on dark matter (DM) coupled to neutrinos focused on $s$-channel annihilation production and $t$-channel scattering. This work investigates a chiral/lepton-number carrying interaction $\bar{\chi}\nu\phi$ where DM production from neutrino annihilation proceeds via $t$-channel exchange, but DM-neutrino scattering proceeds via an $s$-channel resonance with scalar mediator $\phi$. The resulting resonant scattering cross section creates a strong, energy-dependent trapping mechanism that prevents DM escape.
summary.method: The authors compute neutrino-annihilation DM production rates and subsequent DM mean free paths inside a protoneutron star using 1D core-collapse supernova simulation profiles (a $20\,M_\odot$ progenitor at 1 s post-bounce). DM-neutrino scattering incorporates Pauli blocking due to neutrino degeneracy in the core. Energy loss is integrated over the neutrinosphere with an escape condition, and bounds are derived using the Raffelt SN1987A limit ($L_\chi \le 5\times 10^{52}\,\text{erg/s}$).
key_results: For $m_\phi / m_\chi = 3$, an unconstrained window opens for mediator masses between $\sim 5\,\text{MeV}$ and $100\,\text{MeV}$, where resonant scattering traps DM inside the core and completely eliminates the cooling exclusion.

Supernova cooling excludes small mediator masses ($m_\phi \lesssim 5\,\text{MeV}$) and an intermediate high-mass window ($100\,\text{MeV} \lesssim m_\phi \lesssim 300\,\text{MeV}$), above which thermal phase-space suppression shuts off production.
In the non-resonant heavy mediator limit ($m_\phi \sim 10\,\text{GeV}$), the standard effective-operator cooling constraint is recovered.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a clear mechanism where light BSM particles coupled to neutrinos evade standard SN1987A bounds. This directly informs the viable parameter space for neutrino-portal dark sectors and light mediators probed at low-energy neutrino and stopped-pion facilities.
summary.caveats: Assumes any DM that scatters once is trapped and carries away zero net energy (a conservative bound, but neglected energy transport could still deposit heat differentially), and considers flavor-universal couplings without sterile neutrino-antineutrino conversion effects.

papers.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
papers.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.
papers.reason: Presents high-statistics solar neutrino measurements from Super-Kamiokande constraining the solar core size, density, and temperature profile, directly tied to low-energy neutrino programs. [favorite author: Kate Scholberg]

summary.tldr: Super-Kamiokande uses 5805 days of $^8\text{B}$ solar neutrino data and MSW adiabatic conversion to constrain the solar core radius to $< 0.499\,R_\odot$ and determine the central temperature.
summary.novel_idea: Rather than testing neutrino oscillation parameters assuming a fixed Standard Solar Model (SSM), this analysis inverts the problem: it exploits the radial dependence of MSW matter effects and the steep temperature dependence of $^8\text{B}$ production to directly measure solar core parameters (core size, electron density profile, and central temperature) using neutrino observations alone.
summary.method: The analysis uses recoil electron kinetic energy spectra and day/night variations from 5805 days across SK-I through SK-IV. Solar electron density profiles are parameterized under high-metallicity (B16+GS98) and protosolar accretion (K2-A09-MZvar-12) models. Fits are performed on SK data alone and in combination with SNO polynomial survival probability parameters.
key_results: Sets a 90% C.L. upper bound on the solar core size of $0.499\,R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.381\,R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 using SK data alone.
Combined SK + SNO fits tighten the core size limit to $0.268\,R_\odot$ (B16+GS98) and $0.215\,R_\odot$ (K2-A09-MZvar-12).

Measures the solar central temperature as $T_{\text{C}} = (15.599 \pm 0.0016) \times 10^6\,\text{K}$ and temperature at the $^8\text{B}$ production peak as $T_{\text{npz}} = (15.492 \pm 0.0017) \times 10^6\,\text{K}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides an experimental milestone for solar neutrino MSW physics and serves as a benchmark for matter-effect modeling and low-energy solar neutrino detection in water Cherenkov experiments.
summary.caveats: The extracted core size and temperature remain dependent on the adopted baseline composition and opacity models (high vs. low metallicity SSMs).

papers.title: Self-Consistent Subtracted Second Quasiparticle Random-Phase Approximation for Dipole Responses in Neutron-Rich Oxygen Isotopes
papers.abstract: Describing the nuclear dipole response in open-shell nuclei across wide energy scales, from low-lying states below the neutron separation energy to giant resonances near 30MeV, within a single microscopic framework is a long-standing open problem. Here we establish, for the first time, a self-consistent subtracted second quasiparticle random-phase approximation (SSQRPA) that simultaneously incorporates pairing correlations (HF+BCS), explicit two-quasiparticle (2qp) and four-quasiparticle (4qp) configurations in a large model space, the full forward- and backward-going QRPA structure, and a subtraction procedure to eliminate double counting and ensure stability. No existing framework unifies all of these ingredients in the quasiparticle basis. We apply SSQRPA to the dipole excitations of neutron-rich oxygen isotopes $^{18,20,22}$O, where the standard QRPA fails to simultaneously account for high-energy giant dipole resonance (GDR) states near 22--25MeV, medium-energy GDR states in the 10--18MeV region, and isolated low-lying $1^-$ states below the neutron separation energy. In SSQRPA, the dominant isovector (IV) GDR strength shifts downward by approximately 4MeV into the experimentally observed medium-energy region, while the compressional isoscalar (IS) GDR strength remains concentrated at higher energies, in qualitative agreement with the observed electromagnetic dissociation cross sections. For the low-lying states, the root-mean-square deviation from experiment is reduced from 5.31MeV (QRPA) to 0.35MeV (SSQRPA) in $^{18}$O, and from 4.07MeV to 0.74MeV in $^{20}$O, demonstrating that 4qp correlations are essential for a simultaneous description of dipole excitations over a wide range of excitation energies. The SSQRPA provides a powerful and general framework for future microscopic studies of collective excitations in open-shell nuclei across the nuclear mass table.
papers.topic: Subtracted second QRPA for oxygen isotopes
papers.reason: Develops a self-consistent subtracted second quasiparticle random-phase approximation (SSQRPA) for nuclear dipole responses in oxygen isotopes, squarely matching core ab initio and quasiparticle nuclear methods.

summary.tldr: A self-consistent subtracted second QRPA (SSQRPA) incorporating 2qp and 4qp configurations simultaneously resolves the long-standing discrepancy in isovector and isoscalar dipole strength across wide energy scales in neutron-rich oxygen isotopes.
summary.novel_idea: Establishes the first self-consistent second quasiparticle RPA (SSQRPA) for open-shell nuclei that unifies pairing (HF+BCS), full forward/backward QRPA amplitudes, explicit four-quasiparticle (4qp) excitations in a large model space, and an operator subtraction scheme to remove functional double-counting and eliminate dynamical instabilities.
summary.method: Calculations use the SkM* Skyrme energy density functional in the particle-hole channel with a volume pairing force in a harmonic-oscillator basis ($N_{\max} = 12$). The 4qp configuration space includes $2p\text{-}2h$ type quasiparticle states controlled via an occupation probability cutoff $V_{\text{cut}}$. Subtracted QRPA equations are solved for the isovector (IV) and isoscalar (IS) compressional dipole response in $^{18,20,22}\text{O}$.
key_results: In $^{18}\text{O}$ and $^{20}\text{O}$, coupling to 4qp configurations shifts the dominant IV GDR centroid downward by $\sim 4\,\text{MeV}$, directly matching the experimentally observed medium-energy strength at $10\text{--}18\,\text{MeV}$.

Reduces the RMS energy deviation of low-lying $1^-$ states below the neutron separation energy from $5.31\,\text{MeV}$ (QRPA) to $0.35\,\text{MeV}$ (SSQRPA) in $^{18}\text{O}$, and from $4.07\,\text{MeV}$ to $0.74\,\text{MeV}$ in $^{20}\text{O}$.
Demonstrates that high-energy GDR states ($22\text{--}25\,\text{MeV}$) contain substantial IS compressional character, consistent with electromagnetic dissociation data.
summary.why_it_matters: Oxygen isotopes ($^{16}\text{O}$, $^{18}\text{O}$) are key nuclear targets in water Cherenkov detectors (Super-K, Hyper-K). The microscopic incorporation of 4qp correlations provides the exact theoretical framework needed to model multi-nucleon de-excitation, spreading widths, and dipole response functions relevant to neutral-current and low-energy neutrino-nucleus cross sections.
summary.caveats: The current 4qp matrix implementation omits the particle-particle residual interaction channel, and low-lying transition strengths remain smaller than experiment due to the omission of continuum coupling.

papers.title: Probing Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons through EFT-Induced Meson Decays
papers.abstract: We investigate dimension-six operators involving pairs of Dirac-type heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at beam-dump and far-forward experiments. In the $\nu$SMEFT framework, lepton-number-conserving four-fermion operators couple HNL pairs to quarks and induce two and three-body charm and bottom meson decays. We study the $c\to u$, $b\to d$, and $b\to s$ transitions at FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations. HNL production depends on the cut-off scale $\Lambda$, while the lifetime depends on the active-sterile mixing $|V_{eN}|^2$. Sizable production can therefore coexist with the small mixing needed for HNLs to reach distant detectors. We project sensitivities in the $(M_N,|V_{eN}|^2)$ and $(M_N,\Lambda)$ planes, accounting for two and three-body decays and constraints from invisible and semivisible meson decays. SHiP is particularly sensitive to $c\to u$, while the larger FCC-LLP2 configuration probes $b\to d, s$. We find that EFT-induced pair production extends long-lived HNL searches to very small mixing and complements other probes of the $\nu$SMEFT heavy-neutrino sector.
papers.reason:
Investigates $
u$SMEFT dimension-six operators coupling Dirac heavy neutral leptons to quarks and projects sensitivities for beam-dump and far-forward experiments, squarely in the reader's core BSM/neutrino interest.

summary.tldr: Dimension-six $\nu$SMEFT four-fermion operators mediate heavy meson decays into pairs of Dirac heavy neutral leptons, extending displaced-vertex sensitivities at SHiP and FPF to active-sterile mixings well below conventional limits.
summary.novel_idea: Standard heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches link production and decay through the same active-sterile mixing $|V_{\alpha N}|^2$, causing event yields to plummet at small mixing. By utilizing lepton-number-conserving dimension-six four-fermion operators $(\bar{q}q)(\bar{N}N)$, HNL pair production in $c \to u$ and $b \to d, s$ meson decays is governed by $c_{\mathcal{O}}/\Lambda^2$, while decay remains governed by $|V_{eN}|^2$, effectively decoupling production from lifetime.
summary.method: The authors compute two-body ($P \to N\bar{N}$) and three-body ($P \to P'/V + N\bar{N}$) semileptonic decays for $D$ and $B$ mesons across $M_N$. Production kinematics at HL-LHC and FCC-hh are modeled with Pythia 8 rescaled to FONLL cross sections, while SPS fixed-target charm yields are used for SHiP. Geometrical acceptances, boosts, and decay probabilities are simulated for FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations (FCC-LLP1 and FCC-LLP2).
key_results: For $\Lambda = 10\,\text{TeV}$, pair-production displaced-vertex searches probe $|V_{eN}|^2$ down to $10^{-10}\text{--}10^{-12}$ at SHiP ($c \to u$) and $10^{-12}\text{--}10^{-14}$ at FCC-LLP2 ($b \to d, s$), orders of magnitude below existing laboratory limits.
Three-body decays dominate the reach at lower $M_N$, while two-body leptonic modes dictate sensitivity near the kinematic thresholds ($M_N \to m_P/2$).

At fixed mixing $|V_{eN}|^2 = 10^{-10}$, SHiP tests cutoff scales $\Lambda \sim 100\,\text{TeV}$ for charm transitions, while FCC-LLP2 probes $\Lambda \sim 100\text{--}200\,\text{TeV}$ for bottom transitions, significantly surpassing bounds from $B \to K^{(*)}\nu\bar{\nu}$ and invisible meson decays.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts phenomenological studies of forward physics facilities (FPF, FASER2, SHiP) and $\nu$SMEFT phenomenology. It provides an efficient mechanism for generating macroscopic HNL lifetimes while retaining sizable production yields at beam-dump and collider neutrino facilities.
summary.caveats: Assumes zero background and 100% reconstruction efficiency for visible decay modes, and limits active mixing exclusively to the electron-neutrino sector.

papers.title: Emerging understanding of the rare kaon decay $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$ from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Rare kaon decays provide sensitive probes of the Standard Model and potential new physics. For $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$, the experimental decay rate determines only the squared vector form factor $|V(z)|^2$, leaving its sign undetermined. Previous lattice QCD calculations have either used unphysical pion masses or suffered from uncertainties too large to resolve this sign. Here we present a first-principles calculation using two domain-wall fermion ensembles with near-physical pion masses. We develop a computational strategy that establishes the ultraviolet finiteness and continuum equivalence of local and conserved vector currents, substantially simplifying the calculation of nonlocal matrix elements. Four independent subtraction schemes provide nontrivial consistency checks, while the one-end trick reduces noise from quark-self-loop contributions. We determine $V(z)$ at six spacelike and timelike momentum transfers. Fits consistently yield $V(0)<0$, with a statistical significance of $5.8\sigma$--$7.9\sigma$ at $M_{\eta_c}=1.1,\mathrm{GeV}$. After extrapolation to the physical charm-quark mass, the negative sign persists across all fit forms, with a significance of $2.0\sigma$--$3.4\sigma$. Our results provide direct first-principles evidence favoring the negative-sign solution and establish a framework for more precise lattice QCD determinations.
papers.reason: Performs a first-principles lattice QCD calculation of the rare kaon decay $K^+	o\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$ vector form factor sign using near-physical pion masses, matching precision flavor interests.

summary.tldr: A domain-wall lattice QCD calculation near physical pion mass provides the first first-principles evidence that the vector form factor $V(0)$ in $K^+ \to \pi^+ \ell^+ \ell^-$ is negative.
summary.novel_idea: Experimental decay spectra for $K^+ \to \pi^+ \ell^+ \ell^-$ measure only $|V(z)|^2$, leaving a fundamental sign ambiguity in the low-energy constants $(a_+, b_+)$. This work establishes that local vector currents with a subtracted Fourier kernel and GIM cancellation share the identical UV-finite continuum limit as conserved lattice currents, enabling a tractable, noise-reduced lattice calculation of the nonlocal four-point function at near-physical pion mass.
summary.method: Simulations use two RBC/UKQCD domain-wall fermion ensembles with near-physical pion mass ($M_\pi \approx 143\,\text{MeV}$, $a^{-1} = 1.023\,\text{GeV}$ and $1.378\,\text{GeV}$). Exponentially growing single-pion intermediate states are removed via four cross-checked subtraction schemes. Quark-loop noise is suppressed using the one-end trick (even-split method). Form factors are evaluated at six $q^2$ values spanning spacelike and timelike regions, followed by a logarithmic charm-quark mass extrapolation.
key_results: Fits consistently yield $V(0) < 0$ with $5.8\sigma\text{--}7.9\sigma$ significance at $M_{\eta_c} = 1.1\,\text{GeV}$.
Following extrapolation to the physical charm mass, the negative sign solution persists across all polynomial and chiral fit forms with a significance of $2.0\sigma\text{--}3.4\sigma$.
The computed timelike form factor is consistent with the negative branch preferred by chiral perturbation theory ($(a_+, b_+) \approx (-0.58, -0.75)$) and disfavors the positive branch.
summary.why_it_matters: Resolves a long-standing discrete ambiguity in low-energy effective field theory and rare FCNC kaon decays. The computational advances for nonlocal electroweak matrix elements directly map onto precision calculations of second-order weak amplitudes, radiative corrections, and neutrinoless double beta decay kernels.
summary.caveats: Discretization errors (estimated at 10%–20%) are not removed via a continuum extrapolation due to having only two lattice spacings, and the charm mass extrapolation from $M_{\eta_c} \le 1.3\,\text{GeV}$ to the physical point introduces the dominant uncertainty.

papers.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
papers.abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.
papers.topic: Dark matter scattering in superfluid He-3
papers.reason: Provides a first-principles calculation of sub-GeV dark matter scattering using the quantum many-body response of superfluid helium-3, highly relevant to low-threshold nuclear probes.

summary.tldr: A first-principles many-body calculation of light dark matter scattering in superfluid $^{3}\text{He}$ shows that target Fermi-Dirac statistics extend the kinematic recoil tail, improving low-mass detector reach.
summary.novel_idea: The authors extend dynamic structure factor calculations from bosonic $^{4}\text{He}$ and solid-state systems to the B-phase of fermionic superfluid $^{3}\text{He}$. They compute both spin-independent (scalar/density) and spin-dependent (axial-vector/spin-density) responses from first principles. Crucially, they show how Fermi degeneracy kinematics and Bogoliubov quasiparticle pairing break the traditional single-atom scattering approximation near threshold.
summary.method: The differential rate is evaluated via Fermi's Golden Rule using NREFT operators $\mathcal{O}_1$ and $\mathcal{O}_4$. The target response is formulated in BCS mean-field theory where scattering from the quasiparticle vacuum produces two-quasiparticle excitations across the B-phase gap $\Delta_0$. In the rare-event regime where recoil energy $\omega \gg \Delta_0$, the structure functions are evaluated in the degenerate Fermi-gas limit and folded into a profile-likelihood analysis incorporating QUEST-DMC radiogenic backgrounds and SQUID shot noise.
key_results: Finite initial Fermi momentum of the $^{3}\text{He}$ atoms broadens the kinematically allowed recoil spectrum, improving the projected low-mass reach by $\approx 2.5\%$ at the $0.51\text{ eV}$ benchmark threshold relative to the single-atom model.
Demonstrates that lowering the experimental threshold to $5\text{ meV}$ would extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the sub-MeV dark matter mass regime.

Proves that at momentum transfers $q \gg k_F$ (corresponding to $m_\chi \gtrsim 20\text{ MeV}/c^2$ and $E_R > 1\text{ eV}$), the many-body structure function rigorously converges to the incoherent single-atom cross section.
summary.why_it_matters: While targeted at dark matter direct detection, the dynamic structure function formalism for spin-dependent and spin-independent responses in light degenerate nuclear targets directly parallels calculations of low-energy CEvNS and inelastic neutrino-nucleus response functions in condensed or dense environments.
summary.caveats: The calculation treats liquid $^{3}\text{He}$ in the Fermi-gas/mean-field BCS approximation and does not yet incorporate Landau Fermi-liquid interactions or surface-adsorbed quasiparticle states that could modify the response at low temperatures.

papers.title: Improved Bounds on the Dark Matter-Neutrino Cross Section using LSBGs
papers.reason: Derives improved bounds on the dark matter-neutrino scattering cross section using supernova neutrinos and low surface brightness galaxies, directly tied to low-energy neutrino astrophysics.

summary.tldr: Analyzing dark matter core formation from core-collapse supernova neutrino energy injection in Low Surface Brightness Galaxies yields an upper limit of $\sigma_{\nu\chi} < 8.5 \times 10^{-25}\text{ cm}^2$ at $m_\chi = 1\text{ GeV}$.
summary.novel_idea: The paper applies the mechanism where core-collapse supernova (CCSN) neutrinos heat dark matter halos to transform central cusps into cores to Low Surface Brightness Galaxies (LSBGs), which possess much higher stellar masses and larger halos than dwarf spheroidals. Additionally, it corrects earlier counting methods to ensure dark matter particles are not counted multiple times within the single-scattering regime.
key_results: Correcting the overcounting in previous literature weakens the Fornax dSph bound by a factor of $\sim 46$, shifting it to $\sigma_{\nu\chi} < 1.56 \times 10^{-21}\text{ cm}^2$ for $m_\chi < 130\text{ GeV}$.

The LSBG F579-V1 establishes an upper bound of $\sigma_{\nu\chi} < 8.5 \times 10^{-25}\text{ cm}^2$ for $m_\chi \le 35\text{ GeV}$, improving on the corrected dwarf spheroidal bound by roughly three orders of magnitude.
The derived bound is slightly stronger than existing constraints from the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DMDSNB) at $E_\nu \sim 15\text{ MeV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a stringent astrophysical benchmark for MeV-scale neutrino non-standard interactions with dark matter mediators, constraining dark portal models that evade direct laboratory bounds.
summary.caveats: Assumes neutrino scattering is the sole driver of halo flattening, neglecting baryonic feedback outflows; also assumes a flavor-universal neutrino spectrum and central point-source supernova distribution.

papers.title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
papers.abstract: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $\mu_{\Delta}$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.
papers.topic: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.reason: Computes amplitude-dependent bulk viscosity from Urca processes in neutron star mergers, taking thermal blurring and collisional broadening into account, very relevant to dense matter and multi-messenger physics.

summary.tldr: Calculating amplitude-dependent bulk viscosity in neutron star matter with thermal blurring and collisional broadening reveals non-linear viscous enhancements of up to five orders of magnitude for $10\%$ density oscillation amplitudes.
summary.novel_idea: Extends nucleonic bulk viscosity calculations into the suprathermal regime ($|\mu_\Delta| \ge T$) while simultaneously incorporating both thermal blurring of the Fermi surface and in-medium collisional broadening via the Nucleon Width Approximation (NWA). It abandons the traditional odd-power expansion of reaction rates in favor of a complete polynomial expansion in $\mu_\Delta/T$.
summary.method: The authors model non-trapped degenerate $npe$ matter undergoing $1\text{ kHz}$ density oscillations. Net direct and modified Urca re-equilibration rates are computed within the NWA framework across true chemical equilibrium for two equations of state: IUF (with a direct Urca threshold at $n_B = 4.1n_0$) and QMC-RMF3 (no threshold). The chemical imbalance $\mu_\Delta(t)$ is integrated dynamically over the oscillation cycle to extract the net dissipative bulk viscosity.
key_results: Non-linear suprathermal effects become dominant once the density oscillation amplitude $\Delta n / n$ reaches approximately $0.10$.
At low temperatures ($T = 0.5\text{ MeV}$), the bulk viscosity increases by three to five orders of magnitude relative to the subthermal limit for both sub-threshold and super-threshold densities.
At $T = 3\text{ MeV}$, the bulk viscosity remains largely independent of amplitude, confirming that suprathermal enhancements are strictly confined to cooler regions ($T \lesssim 1\text{ MeV}$).
In the subthermal limit, the NWA framework yields a bulk viscosity roughly one order of magnitude larger than standard Fermi-surface modified Urca approximations.
summary.why_it_matters: Although primarily focused on gravitational-wave damping in binary neutron star mergers, the underlying physics involves weak-interaction Urca reaction rates and nucleon spectral broadening in dense matter, touching nuclear many-body response under extreme conditions.
summary.caveats: Assumes neutrinos are completely untrapped ($npe$ matter without trapped lepton number), an assumption that breaks down in hot, dense post-merger cores where neutrino diffusion must be coupled to the fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform
papers.abstract: Active-target gas time projection chambers (TPCs) could provide the ultimate measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future neutrino oscillation measurements. Their development requires optimisation of the gas mixture, pressure, electric fields, and readout configuration. Warwick TPC (WarTPC) is an R\&D platform for investigating in these directions for neutrino physics and beyond. It can operate at pressures up to approximately 10 bar and features a combination of thick gas electron multipliers and a Timepix3 camera for optical readout. In this paper, we present the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform, describing the design and integration of its subsystems, and report the first measurements of its optical response under different operating conditions, demonstrating a stable and functioning R&D platform.
papers.reason: Details the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform using optical readout and high pressures for advanced neutrino interaction measurements.

summary.tldr: The Warwick TPC R&D platform has been constructed and commissioned, demonstrating optical Timepix3 tracking and measuring pressure- and voltage-dependent secondary scintillation up to 7.5 bar in argon gas mixtures.
summary.novel_idea: The paper reports on the design and commissioning of the WarTPC platform: a high-pressure (up to 10 barg) active-target gas TPC specifically dedicated to testing gas mixtures (notably hydrogen-rich mixtures) and optical readout configurations to eliminate nuclear uncertainties in neutrino-nucleus interaction measurements.
summary.method: The system utilizes a 195 L stainless-steel pressure vessel, a 308 mm Delrin field cage producing a $350\text{ V/cm}$ drift field, and an amplification stage consisting of two 1 mm thick THGEMs. Scintillation light shifted by a polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) wavelength shifter (emitting at $\sim 420\text{ nm}$) is focused through an optical viewport onto a Cricket 2 image intensifier coupled to a $256\times 256$ Timepix3 ASIC. Commissioning data were acquired using a $^{241}\text{Am}$ $\alpha$ source and cosmic rays in Ar, $\text{Ar-CH}_4$, and $\text{Ar-CF}_4$ mixtures.
key_results: Achieved first 3D track observations of $5.4\text{ MeV}$ $\alpha$ particles in Ar at $0.4\text{ bar}$ and cosmic rays in $\text{Ar-CF}_4$ (80:20) at $0.1\text{ bar}$.
Quantified THGEM dielectric charging-up time, observing an exponential signal drop with time constant $\tau = 7.2 \pm 1.4\text{ min}$, stabilizing at $61\%$ of initial response.

Measured the normalized optical response up to $7.5\text{ bar}$, observing an exponential gain scaling with reduced electric field $V/p$ and a $\sim 3500$-fold optical suppression between $1\text{ bar}$ and $7.5\text{ bar}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Active-target gas TPCs using hydrogen-rich gas mixtures are central to the long-term neutrino oscillation program (e.g., DUNE near detector concepts) to measure neutrino-hydrogen interactions directly and unsmear nuclear final-state interactions. This platform directly tests optical readout scalability and quenching limitations under high pressure.
summary.caveats: This is an experimental commissioning and hardware paper; full 3D track reconstruction algorithms and systematic studies of high-pressure hydrogenous mixtures (e.g., methane quenching limits on scintillation) are left for future work.

papers.title: Resolving the isospin-mixing anomaly in $^{26}$Si from $^{26}$P $\beta$-decay
papers.abstract: The $\beta$-delayed one- and two-proton emission of the proton-dripline nucleus $^{26}$P provides a sensitive probe of isospin symmetry-breaking. A recent study reported the observation of a strongly isospin-mixed doublet in $^{26}$Si, comprised of the $T = 2$ Isobaric Analog State (IAS) and a state at 13380 keV, yielding a record-high isospin mixing matrix element. We report a new high-resolution measurement of the $^{26}$P $\beta$-delayed charged-particle decay performed at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), shedding new light on the isospin mixing in this decay. By utilizing low-energy beam implantation from the Advanced Cryogenic Gas Stopper (ACGS), we obtained clean one-proton and two-proton decay spectra. Our high statistics study show discrepancies in decay branches and the existence of a 13380 keV state in $^{26}$Si is unsupported by our data. Our deduced branching ratio to the IAS is fully consistent with the expectation from the Fermi sum rule. Consequently, the claim of strong isospin mixing in $^{26}$Si is refuted, reinstating standard theoretical expectations for isospin mixing in nuclei.
papers.reason: Measures $^{26}$P beta-delayed charged-particle decay at FRIB, resolving an isospin-mixing anomaly in $^{26}$Si and restoring standard nuclear expectations.

summary.tldr: A high-resolution FRIB experiment on $^{26}\text{P}$ $\beta$-decay refutes the claimed record-high isospin-mixing doublet in $^{26}\text{Si}$, finding an IAS branching ratio of $4.2(2)\%$ perfectly consistent with the Fermi sum rule.
summary.novel_idea: The study directly re-evaluates the contested decay scheme of the proton-dripline nucleus $^{26}\text{P}$ using stopped, low-energy ion beams instead of high-energy in-flight implantation. This eliminates $\beta$-summing distortions and beam contaminants that previously led Liu et al. (2022) to claim an anomalously large isospin mixing matrix element ($130\text{ keV}$) between the $T=2$ IAS and an alleged state at $13380\text{ keV}$ in $^{26}\text{Si}$.
summary.method: A $30\text{ keV}$ pure beam of $^{26}\text{P}$ delivered by the Advanced Cryogenic Gas Stopper (ACGS) at FRIB was stopped in a thin carbon foil. The decay was monitored by a compact array of segmented $\Delta E-E$ silicon detector telescopes (DSSDs and SSDs) and HPGe detectors, detecting $13,400$ $\beta 2p$ and $470,000$ $\beta p$ events. Kinematic reconstruction was carried out event-by-event including opening-angle-dependent daughter recoil corrections.
key_results: Unambiguously refutes the existence of the reported $13380\text{ keV}$ state in $^{26}\text{Si}$, demonstrating that the $Q_{2p} = 4250\text{ keV}$ peak cited in prior work was an experimental artifact from contaminant $^{25}\text{Si}$ $\beta p \gamma$ decays.
Precisely determines the $^{26}\text{Si}$ IAS excitation energy to be $E_x(\text{IAS}) = 13053(3)\text{ keV}$ from two-proton decay kinematics.

Measures an absolute IAS $\beta$-feeding branch of $4.2(2)\%$ ($3.2(2)\%$ $1p$ and $0.99(12)\%$ $2p$), corresponding to a Fermi transition strength $B = 4.3(2)$, fully matching the superallowed Fermi sum rule expectation of $B_F = 4$ ($3.87(5)\%$) with minimal Gamow-Teller mixing.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts precision tests of electroweak physics and CKM unitarity: it restores theoretical consistency in $sd$-shell isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections ($\delta_C$), which are crucial for extracting $|V_{ud}|$ from superallowed Fermi $\beta$ decays.
summary.caveats: The current dataset does not isolate the proton-$\beta$ angular correlation needed to disentangle the residual Gamow-Teller strength from pure Fermi strength, nor does it observe the isospin-suppressed electromagnetic $\gamma$-decay branch of the IAS.

papers.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $\phi^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
papers.abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $\phi^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.
papers.reason: Simulates real-time scattering and wave packet preparation in scalar field theory on quantum/lattice setups, directly aligning with real-time dynamics and event generator model interests.

papers.title: Unitarity bounds and sum rules in the SMEFT: a systematic analysis
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of perturbative unitarity bounds and spinning sum rules in the baryon-number-conserving dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), with particular emphasis on flavor structure. Employing an on-shell partial-wave formalism for generic $N \to M$ scattering amplitudes, we perform a coupled-channel analysis of the complete operator basis and derive bounds on individual Wilson coefficients by marginalizing over the remaining interactions. We formulate spinning sum rules for four-fermion operators in the Warsaw basis and translate their flavor-space definiteness conditions into constraints on Wilson coefficients, under specified assumptions about the ultraviolet dynamics. We then extend both analyses to the three-generation four-fermion sector within Minimal Flavor Violation, retaining leading up-type Yukawa insertions, and an exact $U(2)^5$ flavor symmetry. The resulting constraints reveal correlations among flavor structures that are absent in the single-flavor limit. Through explicit matching to representative ultraviolet completions, we illustrate how spinning sum rules can distinguish scalar- from vector-mediated interactions, while also identifying the limitations of this interpretation. These results provide a general framework for assessing the consistency of new-physics scenarios within the SMEFT, relying on minimal theoretical assumptions.
papers.reason: Performs a systematic analysis of perturbative unitarity bounds and spinning sum rules in the SMEFT, directly aligning with the reader's high-priority EFT interests.

papers.title: Positivity Bounds, Negative Running, and the Weak Gravity Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study causality and unitarity constraints at one loop on a low-energy effective theory containing a photon, a massless scalar coupled to it through dilaton-like interactions, and a light neutral Dirac fermion with a Yukawa coupling to the scalar. In this setup, non-gravitational loop effects induced by the Yukawa interaction can drive the coefficient of the four-photon $(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})^2$ operator negative at low energies, apparently violating the tree-level positivity bound. Nevertheless, we find that these negative values are consistent with one-loop constraints from causality and unitarity, thanks to the low-energy contribution from the massless scalar to the relevant dispersion relation. We also examine the implications of this negative running for the Weak Gravity Conjecture in the magnetic limit of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes, since the RG-evolved Wilson coefficients can a priori shift the extremality condition towards the subextremal region. We find, however, that this shift is obstructed by the fermion mass induced by the same Yukawa coupling, which prevents the fermion from contributing to the running of the relevant operators down to the low-energy scales required to make the black holes subextremal. Finally, we discuss the relevance of negative running to loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT and to light-by-light scattering in the presence of a light scalar.
papers.topic: Positivity bounds and running in SMEFT
papers.reason: Studies causality and unitarity constraints on low-energy effective theories and discusses implications for loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT.

papers.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
papers.abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

papers.title: $B \to D$ form factors from light-cone sum rules
papers.abstract: We present a light-cone sum rule (LCSR) analysis of the $B\to D$ transition form factors $f_+^{BD}(q^2)$ and $f_0^{BD}(q^2)$ in the large-recoil region, including the next-to-leading-power corrections at tree level. The non-perturbative input is provided by the leading-twist $D$-meson distribution amplitude determined from lattice QCD in the heavy-quark large-momentum effective theory (HQLaMET) framework, which enters together with the twist-three and twist-four distribution amplitudes of the $D$ meson fixed by the QCD equations of motion. A combined fit to the LCSR results at $q^2\lesssim2$~GeV$^2$ and to the FNAL/MILC and HPQCD lattice data at $q^2\gtrsim8.5$~GeV$^2$, performed in the model-independent Boyd-Grinstein-Lebed (BGL) parametrisation, allows us to obtain the form factors over the whole physical range and to extract $|V_{cb}|$ from the semileptonic $B\to D\ell\nu$ decay as well as the lepton-flavour universality ratio $R(D)$.
papers.topic: B to D form factors from LCSR
papers.reason: Computes $B 	o D$ transition form factors using light-cone sum rules and lattice HQLaMET inputs, highly relevant to flavor physics and semi-leptonic decays.

papers.title: Product units in gated recurrent networks enhance prediction of nuclear masses and charge radii
papers.abstract: The prediction of nuclear properties using machine learning can complement theoretical models and advance the exploration of poorly known domains of the nuclear chart. We propose a machine learning technique for predicting nuclear masses and charge radii based on gated recurrent units (GRU) that integrates learnable product-unit mappings into the candidate state to model multiplicative dependencies among neighboring nuclei. Computations are performed in the complex domain to jointly capture amplitude and phase dynamics. Across three data partitions and three training seeds per partition, AM-PU-GRU achieves a mean mass interpolation RMSE of 0.2698 MeV and a temporal RMSE of 0.1905 MeV. Configuration comparisons support the integration of learned products into gated recurrence. Without mass inputs, MI-PU-GRU predicts charge radii with an RMSE of 0.019947 fm, 14.40% below the fixed WS* prior. Matched radius controls further show how candidate fusion shapes the benefit of learned products. Paired errors, nuclide-resolved maps, and inference measurements characterize predictive gains and computational cost. This article is an extended version of our ICCS 2026 conference paper (doi:10.1007/978-3-032-29921-5_10).
papers.topic: Machine learning for nuclear masses and radii
papers.reason: Proposes product units in gated recurrent networks to improve machine learning predictions of nuclear masses and charge radii across the nuclear chart.

papers.title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
papers.abstract: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson. To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $\kappa_\lambda$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $\delta\kappa_\lambda \simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections. The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicio\u{g}lu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $\theta = \pi/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.
papers.reason: Applies quantum state tomography to the Higgsstrahlung process at $e^+e^-$ colliders to constrain Higgs self-coupling and $Z$ anomalous couplings, matching precision BSM interests.

papers.title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Prediction for the Radiative $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ Decay
papers.abstract: We accomplish for the first time the three-loop computation of the photonic radiative jet function in soft-collinear effective theory, which constitutes the last missing and most difficult ingredient for the complete next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD prediction of the simplest radiative $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ decay with an energetic photon at leading power. Importantly, the most prominent three-loop contribution to the radiative bottom-meson decay form factors turns out to arise from the newly determined QCD correction to the jet function rather than from the recently obtained hard correction. We further demonstrate explicitly that our full three-loop calculation of these non-hadronic radiative $B$-meson decay form factors appear to be highly beneficial for an improved extraction of the fundamental shape parameter $\lambda_B$ of the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude.

papers.title: Three-Loop Evolution for Soft Functions of Exclusive $B$-Meson and Higgs Decays
papers.abstract: We bootstrap the complete three-loop Lange--Neubert kernel for the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude in heavy quark effective theory by taking advantage of the conformal symmetry technique. In particular, we provide for the first time an all-order Wilson-line argument for the determination of the constant term in the LN kernel in terms of the light-quark, heavy-quark, and threshold soft anomalous dimensions. Remarkably, this innovative construction requires no additional three-loop diagrammatic calculations. Taking into account further the three-loop QCD evolutions for the hard and hard-collinear coefficient functions, the newly derived three-loop Lange--Neubert equation enables us to manifestly demonstrate the renormalization-group invariance of the soft-collinear factorization formula for the radiative leptonic $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ decay at leading power, validating our bootstrapped three-loop kernel and more importantly, our full bootstrap approach.
papers.reason: Bootstraps the three-loop Lange-Neubert kernel for B-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes, directly complementing high-precision heavy-quark and SCET calculations.

papers.title: RG evolution of the $B$-meson LCDA and radiative jet function at three loops
papers.abstract: We calculate the three-loop evolution kernel of the light-cone distribution amplitude of the $B$ meson, together with the radiative jet function in the leptonic radiative decay $B^-\to\gamma\ell^-\bar\nu$ for the first time. Representing the light-cone distribution amplitude as the discontinuity of a matrix element containing an inverse differential operator, we compute the partonic matrix element in momentum space with a novel method of infrared subtraction. We show that its infrared singularities are governed by the same anomalous dimension as that of the heavy-light quark form factor, so that they can be subtracted without introducing any infrared regulator, thereby preserving gauge invariance and avoiding additional complexity in the Feynman integrals. Based on the renormalization-group invariance of the factorization theorem, we derive the renormalization factor of the radiative jet function, and confirm that it removes all divergences of the bare three-loop radiative jet function. Our results enable the resummation of large logarithms in exclusive $B$ decays at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy.
papers.topic: RG evolution of B-meson LCDA at three loops
papers.reason: Calculates the three-loop evolution kernel of the B-meson LCDA and radiative jet function using infrared subtraction without IR regulators.

papers.title: Light baryon masses from the modified Taylor coupling
papers.abstract: We present a calculation of the positive-parity baryon octet and decuplet spectra, using a non-perturbative interaction governed by the modified Taylor effective charge and complemented by explicit flavour-dependent contributions. The framework transitions seamlessly from the mesonic domain, where it was first established, to the baryonic sector, requiring no further parameter optimization. By solving the relativistic three-body Faddeev equation, we extract both the ground-state masses and amplitudes for the corresponding baryonic configurations. The resulting spectrum reproduces experimental data within a few percent. Additionally, we derive the evolution of the nucleon and $\Delta$ masses as functions of the pion mass, contrast our findings directly against lattice-QCD benchmarks, and evaluate the propagation of the lattice uncertainties into the computed hadronic observables.
papers.topic: Light baryon masses from modified Taylor coupling
papers.reason: Calculates baryon octet and decuplet spectra using Faddeev equations governed by the modified Taylor effective charge, bridging non-perturbative QCD and nuclear physics.

papers.title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
papers.abstract: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_\mu$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $\rho \pi$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

papers.reason:
Constructs $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors via $hoightarrow	ext{pi}$ systems to improve hadronic light-by-light scattering estimates for $(g-2)_
u$, highly relevant to precision electroweak probes.

papers.title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
papers.abstract: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $\theta$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.
papers.reason: Introduces new lightcone GPDs and generalized form factors for QCD with a CP-violating $	heta$-term, extending neutron EDM and 3D nucleon structure studies.

papers.title: Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
papers.abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a $2+2$ pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor $\K=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, with the axis of $\qv$ fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition $\K(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$, and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers.
papers.topic: Ultralight dark matter in gravity gradiometers
papers.reason: Proposes a full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer configuration to measure dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter, perfectly aligning with precision atomic/nuclear probes of new physics.

papers.title: What constrains the neutron-star crust? Present data, future measurements, and EOS doppelg\"angers
papers.abstract: The neutron-star crust plays a central role in pulsar glitches, thermal evolution, and stellar oscillations, yet its properties remain difficult to constrain. We use Bayesian inference with a unified crust-core equation of state to assess what present nuclear and astrophysical data tell us about the crust and what future stellar measurements can add. Within this model, present crust constraints are dominated by chiral effective field theory, with laboratory data providing additional information and current stellar observations having a smaller effect. The adopted theoretical bands determine how tightly the crust properties are constrained, while the treatment of neutron-rich surface energy affects their inferred values. Forecasts centred on a single reference equation of state show that more precise measurements of radius, tidal deformability, and total moment of inertia mainly constrain crust thickness. They provide little additional information about the crust-core transition, crust mass, or crustal moment of inertia and do not recover the precision lost when the chiral effective field theory constraint is removed. Two models with nearly identical global stellar observables can have crust masses and crustal moments of inertia differing by about a factor of two, yet remain indistinguishable at the assumed precision. Precise global measurements therefore need not uniquely determine the crust. Observations that directly probe the crust are needed to distinguish these models.
papers.reason: Uses Bayesian inference with a unified crust-core EOS and chiral EFT to evaluate constraints on neutron-star crust properties and observables.

papers.title: Subleading beauty effects in Higgs production at small transverse momentum
papers.abstract: We study $b$-quark mass effects at small Higgs transverse momentum $q_T$ where the Higgs is produced in gluon fusion via a closed $b$-quark loop. In contrast to top-quark loops, which can be integrated out at a high scale, the $b$-quark mass, $m_b$, induces a second small scale $m_b \sim q_T \ll m_H$ such that standard $q_T$ resummation does not apply in this region, which includes the peak of the distribution. The resummation of mass effects for the $gg\to H$ form factor, which has been studied previously, applies to the $q_T$ spectrum in the limit $q_T \ll m_b$. Unlike this case, for $q_T \sim m_b$, real emissions can resolve the $b$-quark loop, requiring a more complicated simultaneous $m_b$ and $q_T$ factorization. It involves new next-to-leading-power $m_b$ and $q_T$ dependent beam and soft functions, and the corresponding bare factorization theorem suffers - as expected - from endpoint divergences. We use soft-collinear effective theory to explicitly compute all amplitudes with a $b$-quark loop and an additional real soft or collinear emission. Our results provide important insight into the nontrivial structure of the endpoint divergences and show how their expected cancellation happens in the sum of all amplitudes separately for soft and collinear emissions. Interestingly, we find that at this order the endpoint-divergent contributions have a separable dependence on $q_T$ and $m_b$, providing strong motivation that in the future their cancellations can be made manifest in the factorized cross section. As an important further cross check we show that the sum of all SCET amplitudes correctly reproduces the full-QCD one-emission amplitudes expanded in the relevant soft or collinear limit, which also requires nontrivial contributions involving massive Glauber quarks in the effective-theory calculation.
papers.reason: Analyzes $b$-quark mass effects and factorization at small transverse momentum in gluon fusion, touching on advanced soft-collinear effective theory methods.

papers.title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
papers.abstract: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/\epsilon$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.
papers.reason: Traces anomaly-related poles in double deeply virtual Compton scattering to subleading Landau singularities and analyzes infrared prescriptions.

papers.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
papers.abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $\Omega_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $\sigma_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $\sigma_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.
papers.reason: Derives an effective field theory model for joint full-shape analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum, validating on simulations.

papers.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
papers.abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $4.1\sigma$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.
papers.reason: Analyzes the Fading Dark Sector model using DESI full-shape galaxy power spectra and CMB data, extending string-motivated dark energy phenomenology.

papers.title: Efficient Iterative Symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing and hadron applications
papers.abstract: Efficient algorithms for the (anti)symmetrization of quantum registers are necessary for upcoming few- and many-body physics applications, from atomic to particle-physics scales. We propose a recursive algorithm (anti)symmetrizing the last particle added to memory, each time one is created or destroyed, respect to the rest of already (anti)symmetrized ones. Given a generalized Dicke state (GDS) of $(j-1)$ quantum registers, each assigned to a particle, the algorithm produces another GDS of $j$ registers (of $n_{qb}$ qubits each) using a mere $\mathcal{O}(j\log_2^2 j + j n_{qb})$ $\mathtt{CNOT}$ and single-qubit gates, and $3j+\lceil\log_2j\rceil+\mathcal{O}(\max(n_{qb},\log_2 j))$ clean auxiliary qubits. The (anti)symmetrizing operator constructed for this purpose depends on the quantum numbers of the additional particle being introduced or ``created''. The algorithm improves upon the construction presented in Appendix A of \cite{Galvez-Viruet:2024hry} by almost two powers of $j$ and is on par with the most efficient methods to date, while ideally suited for dynamical memory management with variable particle number. We exemplify its applicability with a small selection of problems from hadron physics which are expected to be addressable with upcoming quantum computers.
papers.reason: Proposes an efficient recursive symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing registers, highly relevant to quantum algorithms for nuclear and hadron physics.

papers.title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study possible signatures of the existence of a Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) critical end-point in low-energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions using two-pion femtoscopy. We simulate central $^{209}\mathrm{Bi}+^{209}\mathrm{Bi}$ collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.8$ to 11 GeV using the EPOS 4.0.3 framework, incorporating an equation of state that explicitly includes a critical end-point and is compatible with lattice QCD results at small baryon chemical potentials. We analyze the pion pair-distance distribution and the corresponding two-pion correlation function by fitting them with L\'evy distributions in configuration and momentum spaces, respectively. We find a weak dependence of the source parameters on the collision energy below $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2$ GeV, followed by a change in trend at higher energies, particularly in the intercept parameter $\lambda$. This behavior may be associated with a decreasing fraction of pions coming from the core and an increasing contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Within the present analysis, we do not identify an unambiguous signal attributable to the critical end-point. A comparison with simulations employing different equation of state parameters to vary the strength of the critical point, as well as with simulations without a critical end-point, is necessary to establish the sensitivity of these observables to critical phenomena.
papers.reason: Studies QCD critical end-point signatures using two-pion correlation functions in heavy-ion collisions, adjacent to nuclear equation-of-state studies.

papers.title: Novel observables for exploring jet quenching effects in individual jets
papers.abstract: We introduce event-shape observables in the jet frame to characterize intra-jet shapes and study medium modifications in heavy-ion collisions. Using the JEWEL model, we investigate jet constituent angular and transverse momentum distributions, together with two representative event-shape observables, transverse thrust $\tau_\perp$ and transverse sphericity $S_\perp$, in $p$+$p$ and 0--10% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}$. These observables are evaluated after transforming the jet constituent momenta into the jet frame. The intra-jet shape distributions in Pb+Pb collisions shift toward larger values relative to those in $p$+$p$ collisions, indicating more isotropic distributions of constituent transverse momenta. Comparisons between calculations with and without recoil, along with the dependence on the constituent transverse momentum threshold, indicate that medium response plays an important role in these modifications. These results suggest that jet-frame event-shape observables provide sensitive probes of medium response in jet quenching, complementary to single-particle angular and transverse momentum distributions.
papers.topic: Jet-frame event shapes in heavy-ion collisions
papers.reason: Introduces event-shape observables in the jet frame to probe medium modifications and jet quenching, relevant to parton shower and QCD resummation interests.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
papers.abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $\rho$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $\rho$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $\rho$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.
papers.topic: Gravitational form factors of rho and a1
papers.reason: Computes gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of $ho$ and $a_1$ mesons in a holographic QCD model, connecting to hadron structure.

papers.title: ESME stays positive: event generation with positive weights
papers.abstract: Fully differential simulations of hard-scattering processes are a cornerstone of precision phenomenology at collider experiments. For long, Monte Carlo event generators have been able to achieve next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy, but their results typically suffer from the presence of negative-weight events. These degrade statistical power and complicate downstream analyses. In this contribution, we present Exponentiated Subtraction for Matching Events (ESME), a novel approach to NLO+PS matching that yields positive-definite event weights while preserving perturbative accuracy and the logarithmic structure of the shower. We discuss the formalism and its implementation within the PanScales framework.
papers.reason: Presents a novel approach to NLO+PS matching yielding positive-weight events in the PanScales framework, useful for event generator development.

papers.title: Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics?
papers.abstract: In this work, we perform a systematic Bayesian analysis of the full parameter space of a state-of-the-art hybrid hydrodynamical model and show that no combination of parameters provides a satisfactory description of the low-$p_T$ region of the pion $(\pi^{\pm})$ transverse-momentum spectra. This suggests that an additional mechanism enhancing pion production at low $p_T$ may be needed to properly describe the ALICE data. We first reexamine and confirm the existence of an excess of low $p_T$ pions relative to model predictions, showing that no comparable excess is observed in the spectra of kaons $(K^\pm)$, protons $(p)$, or antiprotons $(\bar{p})$. We further demonstrate that this excess persists under a rigorous Bayesian analysis of simulations that include, e.g., a hadronic afterburner, a feature omitted in previous similar studies. Despite the observed excess, the scaled pion spectra retain their universal behavior, exhibiting little dependence on collision centrality. In fact, pions exhibit the most pronounced universality among the particle species considered. We then estimate the effects of two candidate mechanisms for generating the low-$p_T$ pion enhancement by introducing a one-parameter extension of the model into the Bayesian analysis. We find that the data favor enhancement mechanisms whose contributions decrease with increasing $p_T$, becoming negligible at high-$p_T$. Our results motivate further investigations of non-equilibrium effects in hybrid hydrodynamic simulations.
papers.reason: Performs Bayesian analysis on hybrid hydrodynamic models to address low-$p_T$ pion spectra excesses in heavy-ion collisions, touching on hadronic transport and low-energy dynamics.

papers.title: Connecting High-Twist Expansion and Color Glass Condensate Dynamics
papers.abstract: The high-twist (HT) expansion and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) describe nuclear multiple scattering in complementary kinematic regimes. For direct-photon production in proton-nucleus collisions, we formulate an arbitrary-order multiple-scattering master expression that includes photon emission before, between, or after the ordered quark scatterings in the amplitude and its conjugate. In the high-energy limit, resumming multiple scatterings to all orders recovers the CGC Wilson-line dipole result. However, the naive power expansion of the eikonal CGC result reproduces the leading twist but only part of the twist-four contribution obtained in the HT expansion. Including longitudinal sub-eikonal phases and Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference restores the CGC-HT correspondence through twist-4.
papers.reason: Connects high-twist expansion and Color Glass Condensate dynamics for multiple scattering in nuclear collisions, relevant to high-energy nuclear DIS.

papers.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
papers.abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.
papers.reason: Proposes a superconducting gravity gradiometer to detect composition-dependent ULDM, intersecting with precision atomic and nuclear probes of new physics.
